body.statement: If \(\mathcal I_{n,\alpha}\) covers \((r_{bt},q_w)\) simultaneously with probability at least \(1-\alpha\), then with the same probability \(\mathcal V(p_{BT},q)\subseteq\widehat{\mathcal V}_{n,\alpha}\) and \(\mathcal M^\star\subseteq\widehat{\mathcal M}_{n,\alpha}\). Both inclusions hold without uniqueness, strict Hall slack, or separation between policy regrets, and the sets are computable by finite-dimensional optimization over explicitly given polytopes.
body.justification: Set inclusion avoids differentiability of active faces and provides honest simultaneous coverage at Hall and policy ties.
body.gap: JanvinRyalenSarvetStensrud2025 reports a one-sided bootstrap bound for one threshold, while ChernozhukovHongTamer2007 and Gafarov2025 do not combine censoring-adjusted margins, a random Hall polytope, and a set-valued regret optimizer.
body.consumer: A capped switching analysis can report one confidence object covering every compatible value vector and every robust threshold.
